exposure: Use of Intra-Uterine Device (IUD) contraceptive methods
Increasing the number of antenatal visits
outcome: Cesarean section (CS) delivery compared to normal vaginal delivery (NVD)
cohort: 300 Palestinian women (150 who had a CS and 150 who had a NVD) were selected from three hospitals.
finding: The study identified several obstetric and non-obstetric risk factors significantly associated with an increased likelihood of cesarean section, including overweight, various pregnancy complications, previous CS, and the use of pregnancy fixatives, while exercise and increased antenatal visits were associated with avoiding CS.
mod_finding: Factors such as overweight before/during pregnancy, specific pregnancy complications (edema, anemia, bleeding, high blood pressure), mal-presentation, previous CS, advanced gestational age, and use of pregnancy fixatives were significantly associated with an increased risk of CS.
cross-section timing: Data was collected through face-to-face interviews with participants who recently gave birth, assessing risk factors before and during pregnancy relative to their mode of delivery.
